'''Christopher M. Wood''' [[Royal Society of Canada|FRSC]] is an adjunct professor of zoology at the University of British Columbia and a Lifetime Distinguished University Professor, and emeritus Professor of Biology at [[McMaster University]]. He is also a research professor at the University of Miami. His research is primarily concerned with [[Fish physiology]] and aquatic toxicology.

He was educated at the [[University of British Columbia]] (BSc, 1968; MSc, 1971) and the [[University of East Anglia]] (PhD, 1974).<ref>{{cite book|title=Toxicity of Dietborne Metals to Aquatic Organisms}}</ref> He joined the faculty of [[McMaster University]] in 1976 where he was a [[Canada Research Chair]] in Environment and Health from 2001 to 2014. In 2014 he retired from McMaster University and moved to the University of British Columbia, where his research program is now based. He was made a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Canada]] in 2003, and was awarded the 2007 [[Miroslaw Romanowski Medal]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Battling pollution in coastal areas|url=http://www.idrc.ca/EN/Programs/Science_and_Innovation/IDRC_Challenge_Fund/Pages/Battling-pollution-in-coastal-areas.aspx|website=[[International Development Research Centre]]|access-date=2 October 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006112133/http://www.idrc.ca/EN/Programs/Science_and_Innovation/IDRC_Challenge_Fund/Pages/Battling-pollution-in-coastal-areas.aspx|archive-date=6 October 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Past Award Winners|url=https://rsc-src.ca/en/past-award-winners|website=[[Royal Society of Canada]]|access-date=2 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160602175348/http://rsc-src.ca/en/past-award-winners|archive-date=2 June 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was also awarded the [[Fry Medal]] of the Canadian Society of Zoologists in 1999.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nature Honors Dr. Chris M. Wood|url=http://globe.setac.org/2010/december/chris-wood.html|access-date=2 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006093833/http://globe.setac.org/2010/december/chris-wood.html|archive-date=6 October 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>
